merged.title: feat(launcher): scaffold a desktop launcher for all four games
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
A Tauri 2 desktop app in `launcher/` that puts OpenRAC behind buttons for every version in `games/` (rac1 PAL and NTSC-U, rac2, rac3, rac4): find your discs, place each build's inputs, set up, build, check, play in PCSX2, and open the level editor. It runs the checkout's own tools and streams their output; it hard-codes nothing a `game.json` already says.

This is **scaffolding**: the app, its look, the catalogue, the job runner and the repository-wide actions work; most per-game actions are written from each game's docs but not yet run from the launcher. `launcher/docs/INTEGRATION.md` is the handoff for connecting them.

## What's in it

- **`launcher/core/`** (Rust, no window): the catalogue from `games/*/game.json` and `progress/summary.json`; each version's disc and input status (names, sizes, links; never hashes an image); settings; detection of the checkout, Python, PCSX2, Godot and Docker; a job runner that streams output and cancels a job's whole process tree.

opened.title: Native port scaffolding: no emulation, OpenGOAL-style set-up, port/ with hostgen, runtime, renderer and openrac-rac1
opened.author: Veradictus
opened.untrustedBody:
## Summary

This takes OpenRAC from "play through emulation" to the scaffolding of a **native PC port, built the way OpenGOAL ported Jak and Daxter, for every game version**. It has three parts:

1. **No emulation.** The emulator experiment (`runtime/`) is removed. Its studies are kept in `docs/port/`, and git history keeps the code (for example at `7954152`). The launcher no longer imports ISOs or runs anything emulated.
2. **OpenGOAL's disc set-up.** `tools/extractor.py` copies and validates the player's disc, using OpenGOAL's folder layout and error numbers. The launcher's "Set up from your disc" runs it.
3. **`port/`**, the native port's code. Every version in `port/game/` is built from its decompilation into `openrac-<id>`:

merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

Promote five canonical shared call bodies into the boot unit and 26 native overlay units, and publish their freshly qualified proofs. The five bodies reproduce 375 measured placements: a 100-byte body that derives a 16-byte element at index-1 from its index-2 and index-3 neighbours through two bound helpers (215 placements), and 592, 484, 288 and 228-byte bodies whose original game role is unknown (27, 27, 52 and 54 placements). Generated spelling, whitespace and declarations are preserved, so object provenance stays valid. Barlow is the only program with no placement; its small-data unit keeps its current profile and source.

- Validated base: 5c7206289

merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

Adopt the folded-zero-store compiler identity as the qualified C chain and re-qualify the whole published corpus on it. `cc1` moves from `8bed6eae` to `5fed4e23`; `cpp` and GNU `as` keep their hashes, so only the compiler half of the instrument identity changes.

The retired `allow_zero_ti_store.patch` admitted constraint `J` on the register alternatives of `movti_internal` and printed them with `%z1`, which folded a 128-bit zero into its store. It earned no witness of its own: the control sources that store a zero through a `mode(TI)` pointer — including the `FUN_00282C88` spelling — are byte-identical with and without it, because it only ever moved the memory alternatives, which already accepted `J`. Its real effect was to suppress the register form the retail uses whenever one materialised zero feeds several stores. opened.author: llesieur99

## Summary

Adopt the folded-zero-store compiler identity as the qualified C chain and re-qualify the whole published corpus on it. `cc1` moves from `8bed6eae` to `5fed4e23`; `cpp` and GNU `as` keep their hashes, so only the compiler half of the instrument identity changes.

The retired `allow_zero_ti_store.patch` admitted constraint `J` on the register alternatives of `movti_internal` and printed them with `%z1`, which folded a 128-bit zero into its store. It earned no witness of its own: the control sources that store a zero through a `mode(TI)` pointer — including the `FUN_00282C88` spelling — are byte-identical with and without it, because it only ever moved the memory alternatives, which already accepted `J`. Its real effect was to suppress the register form the retail uses whenever one materialised zero feeds several stores.
